body:
N-27 SLICES 2c, 2b, 2e, 2d: ONE DESIGN, PART 2 OF 2 (continues part 1).

2e (SERVER, one line + tests): once 2b is merged the janitor drops the file_history clause, so an ex-file ref is retirable under the same rule as junk and the tombstone tells the phone. KEEP the age-bounded keep ("a file change in the last 14 days", the clause the first version of 2a had): harmless, and a phone that reads the feed between a prune and the retirement hears `file: null` first. REMOVAL TRIGGER of file_history = 2b merged AND an away-phone test extended (cursor taken before, janitor run past 14 days, the feed with goneSince lists the ref).

2d (SERVER, after 2e): make the refs of DELETED playlists and of imports retirable.
* library.changes answers for a playlist or entry whose row is MISSING with the tombstone shape ({id, deleted: true}) instead of skipping it, as likes already do ("removed": item is None). The phone parses tolerantly (readString(...) ?? ''): to be PROVED by a test against applyPlaylists. Then tombstoned playlists and entries can be PURGED after 90 days (the change_log rows stay: they only say "touched").
* An import keeps its counts on the import row; its import_entry rows are purged 60 days after it is done (an old import's page shows counts, not songs: a product line to confirm with the drawing of the import page; until then 2d purges no import).
* After the purge their refs have no pointer, the janitor retires them and ref_gone tells the phones. Without 2d these refs are bounded by what people delete (VM 108 shows it: the 29 refs of a deleted test playlist stay).

ORDER AND COST: 2c (additive, no behaviour change for any phone) -> 2b (phone, behind the feature string) -> 2e (one line) -> 2d. Four small PRs, each tests-first, each read by the advisor before the merge. A migration number must not collide with N-26 slice 2's (it adds columns to song_ref): take the next free number when branching. N-27 is marked built only after 2c, 2b and 2e; 2d is hygiene of an unbounded but small table: record it as its own board item then. Cost of NOT doing them: the table keeps every ref that ever held a file (hundreds to a few thousand rows for an active library): fine for the first public image, and the item stays open, said honestly. NONE of this gates the first public image (unlike N-26 slices 1 and 2).

OPEN FOR THE ADVISOR: (1) tombstone every retired ref or only ex-file refs (junk rows on a phone would then need the age rule)? I chose every ref: one rule, one signal, tiny rows. (2) 90 and 60 days for 2d: fixed numbers, not Host settings? (3) Does 2b need a drawing? I think not: nothing new is visible.
